settings.question: What are aluminium lugs, and how are they different from the standard road kit?
settings.answer: On our standard road kit you wrap each joint by hand with flax fibre and epoxy. This flagship kit instead joins the bamboo with pre-formed aluminium lugs — ready-shaped aluminium sockets the tubes bond into. They give a cleaner, more uniform joint, a lighter and stiffer frame, and a faster, more forgiving build. It's the same endurance road geometry and the same bamboo ride feel — just the premium construction.

settings.question: Are aluminium lugs really lighter and stiffer than wrapped joints?
settings.answer: Yes — that's the whole point of the lugged build. Pre-formed aluminium lugs are lighter and torsionally stiffer than the equivalent hand-wrapped fibre joint, so more of your power goes to the back wheel and the finished frame is the lightest road frame we make. You still keep bamboo's natural vibration damping for all-day comfort — you're sharpening the joints, not deadening the ride.

settings.question: Is it stiff and efficient enough for fast road riding?
settings.answer: Bamboo frame tubing tested at Swansea University to BS ISO 22157:2019 — 84.3 MPa ultimate tensile, comparable to mild steel at a fraction of the weight. That figure is for the tubing we supply, not for a finished frame: how strong your bike ends up is decided by your joints. Follow the manual, let the resin cure fully, and check the joints before every early ride — and call us if anything looks wrong.

settings.question: Why is the lugged road kit more than the standard road kit?
settings.answer: The pre-formed aluminium lugs are a premium component — they cost more to produce than a reel of flax fibre, and they deliver the lighter, stiffer, cleaner-finished flagship frame. You're paying for the lug construction and the result. If you'd rather hand-wrap your joints and save, the standard Road kit is the same geometry and ride feel at a lower price.

settings.question: Will the frame survive years of big road miles?
settings.answer: Finished frames are sealed with epoxy resin. Dry your bike after wet rides, store it indoors, and check the joints before every early ride. The tubing we supply is tested at Swansea University to BS ISO 22157:2019; how your bike holds up over the years is decided by the joints you make — follow the manual and let the resin cure fully, and call us if anything ever looks wrong.
